title: Stage 2: A naive Dockerfile
summary: Get the API running in a container the simplest way, then measure what that costs.

steps.title: The simplest thing that works
body: It works. It also ships the **entire SDK** (compilers, MSBuild, NuGet caches, your source) and re-downloads every NuGet package whenever any file changes, because `COPY . .` comes before the restore that `publish` does.

steps.prompt: Why does the `docker run` above publish `-p 8080:8080`, not `-p 8080:80`?
options: .NET 8+ images listen on port 8080 by default (so they can run as non-root)
steps.explain: `ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS` defaults to 8080 in the official images.

steps.prompt: The database runs on the developer's machine, not in a container. Why `Host=host.docker.internal` and not `localhost`?
options: Inside the container, localhost is the container itself; host.docker.internal resolves to the host on Docker Desktop
steps.explain: In stage 4 the database moves into Compose and the host becomes the service name `db`.

steps.prompt: The container is running. What does this print?
steps.explain: Name, then the published mapping: all host interfaces, port 8080, to container port 8080 over TCP.

steps.prompt: Match each problem of the naive image to its consequence.
pairs: an image of roughly 900 MB with compilers inside
every code edit re-downloads all NuGet packages
bin/obj and .git are sent and copied into the image

steps.title: Build the naive image and measure it
prompt: This terminal has a **real Docker Engine** with the **.NET 10 SDK image** already loaded (no network). `~/todo`
holds the TodoApi and a first, naive `Dockerfile`: one stage on the full SDK. Read it, then:
1. build it as `todo:naive` and run it as a container named `todo`, publishing the API's port (ASP.NET Core in the
official images listens on **8080**) on this machine's `8080`; `curl http://localhost:8080/health` prints `ok`;
2. write the image's size in whole MB (`docker image inspect -f '{{.Size}}'` gives bytes; divide by 1,000,000)
into `~/answers/naive-mb.txt`, and the SDK base image's size the same way into `~/answers/sdk-mb.txt`.
The build takes a minute: `dotnet publish` runs inside it.

checks.name: todo runs from todo:naive and answers /health
checks.fail: There is no container `todo` from `todo:naive` answering `http://localhost:8080/health`. `-p 8080:8080`.

checks.name: naive-mb.txt is the image's size
checks.cmd: a=$(xargs < ~/answers/naive-mb.txt); b=$(( $(docker image inspect -f '{{.Size}}' todo:naive) / 1000000 )); echo "you: $a, Docker: $b"; [ $(( a - b )) -le 2 ] && [ $(( b - a )) -le 2 ]
checks.fail: Not the image's size in MB. `docker image inspect -f '{{.Size}}' todo:naive`, divided by 1,000,000.

checks.name: sdk-mb.txt is the base image's size
checks.cmd: a=$(xargs < ~/answers/sdk-mb.txt); b=$(( $(docker image inspect -f '{{.Size}}' mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0-alpine) / 1000000 )); echo "you: $a, Docker: $b"; [ $(( a - b )) -le 2 ] && [ $(( b - a )) -le 2 ]
checks.fail: Not the SDK image's size in MB. `docker image inspect -f '{{.Size}}' mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0-alpine`.

hints: `docker build -t todo:naive ~/todo`, then `docker run -d --name todo -p 8080:8080 todo:naive`.
`docker image inspect -f '{{.Size}}' todo:naive` prints bytes; `echo $(( BYTES / 1000000 ))` makes MB.
`echo $(( $(docker image inspect -f '{{.Size}}' todo:naive) / 1000000 )) > ~/answers/naive-mb.txt`, and the same for the SDK image.
steps.explain: The naive image works, and that is its trap: it ships the whole SDK (compilers, NuGet, MSBuild) plus the source code, to run one small DLL. Almost all of its size is the base image. Every one of those megabytes is pulled on every deploy and scanned for vulnerabilities, and the compilers are tools an attacker would love to find. The next stage fixes it.
